name: Auction Poker
description: Auction Poker is a dynamic Stud variant where the primary mechanic is 'buying' improved position or cards from a communal marketplace. Unlike standard poker where you are dealt what you get, Auction Poker allows players to actively purchase cards from a face-up display or the top of the deck, paying a premium to the pot to refine their hand before betting rounds.

overview.description: Auction Poker is a dynamic Stud variant where the primary mechanic is 'buying' improved position or cards from a communal marketplace. Unlike standard poker where you are dealt what you get, Auction Poker allows players to actively purchase cards from a face-up display or the top of the deck, paying a premium to the pot to refine their hand before betting rounds.

history.origins: Emerging from the 'Dealer's Choice' tradition in American home games, Auction Poker (and its sibling 'Buy Your Card') was designed to increase pot sizes and reduce the impact of purely random distribution.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Variations of 'Buying' poker appear in military and fraternal card clubs.
1980s: Cataloged by card game historians as a distinct sub-genre of 'Exchange' poker.
Present: A popular specialty game in high-stakes home games where 'The Market' is used to induce action.
history.cultural: Often played as a 'High-Low' game to maximize participation and split pots.
history.evolution: Evolution from static Stud to 'Market-based' Stud increased the skill ceiling by requiring players to value card improvements against the cost in chips.

setup.players: 2-6 players (to ensure enough cards in the deck for buying rounds).
setup.dealing: Initial: 2 cards face down, 3 cards face up to each player. Market: 3 cards dealt face up in a row in the center.

rules.objective: Form the best five-card poker hand using your hole cards and purchased improvements.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Initial Deal**: Players receive 5 cards (2 down, 3 up). 2. **Buying Round**: Starting left of dealer, each player may: (a) Buy a card at the fixed price, discard one of their current cards face down, and take the new card; (b) Pass. 3. **Replacement**: If a market card is bought, it is immediately replaced from the deck. 4. **Betting Round**: A standard round of poker betting follows each buying round. 5. **Cycles**: There are typically 3 buying rounds followed by 3 betting rounds. 6. **Showdown**: Standard poker hand rankings apply.
keyRules: Purchased units are added to the pot immediately and do not count as 'bets' (others don't have to match them).
If you buy a card, you MUST discard one. You always maintain a 5-card hand.
High-Low Split: Often played where the highest and lowest (A-5) hands split the pot.

strategy.basic: Don't pay for cards that only marginally improve your hand's strength. Buying a '4' to make a pair is rarely worth 2 units.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Open Market' read: Watch what your opponents buy. If someone buys a face-up 10 and they already have a 10 showing, you know they have at least three of a kind.
strategy.advanced: Value Betting the Market: If you have a strong hand, use the buying rounds to build the pot size without looking aggressive. The chips you pay to the market grow the pot for when you eventually win at showdown.
tips: The '4-unit' blind draw from the deck is a gamble; only take it if the face-up market cards are useless and you are desperate for a draw.
Pay attention to 'The Replacement'. If the dealer flips a high Spade after you buy a card, and the next player is chasing a flush, you've just improved their odds.

variations.name: Auction Flop
variations.description: Players bid against each other for the right to take cards from a community flop.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Auction Flop is described in sources but its flop-bidding changes are not modeled as engine overrides yet.

variations.name: Market Wilds
variations.description: If a Joker appears in the market, its price is doubled, but it acts as a wild card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Market Wilds introduces jokers and wild-card behavior; engine overrides for wild cards are not represented yet.

scoring.description: Standard Poker Hand Rankings (High or High-Low).
scoring.winCondition: Capturing the pot at showdown or by forcing all others to fold.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated Stud variant where players buy individual cards from a face-up marketplace. Optimize your poker hand by paying the premium, manage your bankroll against the market costs, and dominate the showdown in this high-action classic.

hero.title: AUCTION POKER
hero.subtitle: The Market Always Wins
hero.tagline: Don't just play the hand you're dealt. Buy the hand you want.
